title: Anderson orthogonality scaling in the Rabi-driven heavy Fermi polaron
authors: Michael Rautenberg, Tobias Krom, Eugen Dizer, Olivier Bleu, Eleonora Lippi, Tilman Enss, Manfred Salmhofer, Lauriane Chomaz, Matthias Weidemüller
abstract: The Anderson orthogonality catastrophe (AOC) is a paradigmatic many-body phenomenon in which a local perturbation induces a macroscopic response of a Fermi sea. We probe signatures of the AOC by coherently driving heavy Fermi polarons in an ultracold $^6$Li-$^{133}$Cs mixture. We observe a power-law dependence of the measured Rabi frequency on the drive strength, with exponents consistent with AOC predictions. Finite-temperature simulations quantitatively reproduce the observed scaling, indicating that AOC signatures persist beyond the idealized zero-temperature, infinite-mass limit. The damping of the Rabi oscillations provides access to polaron dephasing and reveals a nonmonotonic drive dependence, qualitatively consistent with current theories. Our results establish coherently driven impurities as a versatile probe of quantum many-body dynamics through local coherent control.
summary: This paper uses ultracold Fermi polarons to experimentally probe the Anderson Orthogonality Catastrophe (AOC) by coherently driving the system. The authors observe that the Rabi frequency reduction follows the predicted power-law scaling of the AOC, confirming that driven impurities are excellent tools for studying complex quantum many-body dynamics. The work successfully bridges theory and experiment in the context of strongly interacting quantum gases.
main_problem: The study investigates the signatures of the Anderson Orthogonality Catastrophe (AOC) in a dynamically driven many-body system.
main_result: The measured Rabi frequency exhibits a power-law scaling consistent with AOC predictions, confirming that coherently driven impurities serve as a versatile probe for quantum many-body dynamics.
method: The research combines experimental measurements on ultracold atomic mixtures with detailed theoretical modeling using T-matrix and FDA approaches.
model_or_system: The system is a heavy Fermi polaron (impurity) immersed in a non-interacting Fermi sea, realized using an ultracold mixture of $^{6}	ext{Li}$ and $^{133}	ext{Cs}$ atoms, driven by optical Raman spectroscopy.
key_observables: Rabi frequency ($\Omega$), damping rate ($\Gamma$), and the ratio $\Omega/\Omega_0$ as functions of drive strength and interaction strength.
important_parameters: Finite temperature ($T/T_F = 0.25$), drive strength ($\hbar\Omega_0$), and impurity-bath mass ratio ($M/m$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing experimental data to theoretical frameworks like the full T-matrix theory, acknowledging that finite temperature causes small deviations from ideal zero-temperature AOC predictions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the power-law scaling of $\Omega/\Omega_0$ vs. drive strength, comparisons of $\Omega$ and $\Gamma$ vs. interaction strength, and the dependence of these quantities on temperature and mass ratio.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares experimental measurements of Rabi oscillations and damping rates against multiple theoretical models (FDA, T-matrix) to extract the AOC scaling exponent and analyze finite-temperature and mass-ratio effects.
why_interesting: This work provides a clean, controllable platform (ultracold atoms) to observe a fundamental many-body phenomenon (AOC) using local coherent control, bridging quantum optics, many-body physics, and cold atom techniques.
